intro.lead: Every unit you build is a reusable, ready-made team.
intro.body: Set one up from a template or from scratch, then assign it to as many projects as you like — agents are shared across projects.

templates.summaryWithUnits: {{units}} and {{agents}} will be created with job descriptions, skills and permissions ready to go. You can edit them all later and assign the unit to any projects you like.

projects.desc: In projects this unit is assigned to, all members of the unit and its sub-units take part.

danger.title: Delete unit
danger.root: The organization root can't be deleted.
danger.desc: Agents aren't deleted; only their memberships in these units are removed, and the units are removed from projects.
danger.descWithSubs_one: {{count}} sub-unit will be deleted too. Agents aren't deleted; only their memberships in these units are removed, and the units are removed from projects.
danger.descWithSubs_other: {{count}} sub-units will be deleted too. Agents aren't deleted; only their memberships in these units are removed, and the units are removed from projects.

export.title: Share
export.descUnit: Save this unit with everything under it (sub-units, agents, titles, skills) as a .agentbits file to send to a friend. API keys, connection details, tasks and chat are never included; connections and apps appear by name only, as a setup note.
export.descAgent: Save this agent (profile, job description, skills, suggested provider) as a .agentbits file to send to a friend. API keys, connection details, tasks and chat are never included; connections and apps appear by name only, as a setup note.

import.title: Import a package
import.intro: Open a .agentbits file someone shared with you, or paste a GitHub link to one. You'll see everything in it before anything is added.
import.trust: Read the job descriptions and personas before importing: they become your agents' instructions. Imported agents always start with "Ask for approval" on, get no extra folders, and need their connections and apps set up by you.
import.needs: Used these connections / apps (set up your own and grant access): {{names}}
import.suspicious: Looks like an instruction to the model — check it
import.reused: These skills were already installed, so yours were kept: {{names}}

learn.title: Learning from chat
learn.desc: When you tell an agent something lasting about yourself or how the team should work, it can remember it for the whole organization. Only your own chat messages count — never files, web pages or reports.
learn.askHint: Each new memory waits for your yes.
learn.autoHint: Saved right away; you can edit or forget it here.

memory.graphHint: Drag to move, scroll to zoom, click a dot for details.
memory.listHint: Search, edit or forget any memory.

profile.title: Knows you
profile.desc: Every agent is told this about you.
profile.empty: Nothing yet. Tell an agent how you like to work, or add it here.

memory.youDesc: You. Preferences point here: every agent is told them.
memory.graphTruncated: the most important 300 memories are drawn
memory.graphEmpty: Memory is empty. As the team works and you chat, memories and their links appear here.
memory.supersededDesc: A newer memory replaced this one. It stays as history and is no longer sent to agents.

projectNotes.title: Project memory notes
projectNotes.desc: Agents add notes to the project memory folder (.agentbits/memory) when they learn something worth keeping or you ask them to remember it. They only append; your own text is never replaced. Turn the folder on or off per project in the project settings.
projectNotes.askHint: Each note waits for your yes.
projectNotes.offHint: Agents read the folder but don't write to it.
